label: DAY 2
title: A viewer left one word: engagement. Here's what YouTube actually counts.

scenes.label: the first comment on my channel
lines: The first comment on my channel was one word. Engagement.
It came from Baroochi Y T. So I looked up what YouTube actually counts.

scenes.title: My first real numbers
lines: First, my own numbers. My first Short got twenty eight views in about twelve hours.
Episode one, the long video, got eleven.

scenes.label: average viewed on my Short
lines: On average, people watched forty one point seven percent of that Short.
About twenty five seconds out of sixty.

scenes.title: What YouTube says shapes recommendations
lines: YouTube's help page lists what shapes recommendations.
What you watch and search, who you subscribe to, and what you like.
Surveys that ask whether you were satisfied.
And dislikes, not interested, and don't recommend channel push videos away.

scenes.sub: YouTube's help page doesn't mention them
lines: Here's the surprise. That page doesn't mention comments at all.

scenes.title: What counts as a view now
log: view: counts from the first frame
lines: Views changed too. Since late August, a view counts from the very first frame, even on autoplay.
An engaged view means someone kept watching past the first few seconds.
And engaged views are what count toward earning money.

scenes.sub: Me: yes. This video came from one word.
lines: So does commenting help? For the algorithm, YouTube's page doesn't say.
For me, yes. This whole video came from one word. Leave one, and it might become day three.
